newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Kabila jets to S.Africa to consult Mandela.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kabila jets to S.Africa to consult Mandela.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila left Lubumbashi airport for South Africa on Wednesday to meet President Nelson Mandela, eyewitnesses said.

Kabila departed at 11.40 a.m. (0940 GMT) on a South African Air Force jet bound for Cape Town after a two-day visit to Zaire's second largest city to mark his rebels' capture of the mineral-rich Shaba province.
Speaking to reporters at the airport, he again asserted that nothing would halt his drive to unseat Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
"There will no ceasefire until Mobutu relinquishes power," the rebel leader said.
Kabila was due to meet Mandela for consultations on the Zaire conflict. South African government officials declined any comment.
Regional analysts said the South Africa talks would centre on arrangements for a face-to-face meeting between Kabila and Mobutu.
South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo on Tuesday predicted dramatic progress within days in ending the civil war in Zaire and said Kabila could visit soon.
Kabila had remained in seclusion in Lubumbashi since his arrival on Monday.
The rebels now control more than half of Africa's third largest country, and Kabila says he is targeting the capital Kinshasa in a bid to drive the ailing Mobutu from power.
